explanations: There is none. Each source's own cursor and any already-fetched but unreturned items are carried inside the merged cursor, so nothing is skipped or repeated between pages. A source is only refetched when its buffer is below limit, buffers are kept sorted with the same total order (createdAt desc, id tie-break) used for the k-way merge, and nextCursor is null only when every source is exhausted and fully drained. Malformed or mismatched cursors are rejected rather than silently restarting.

Unreturned items remain in state.B.buffer, which encode serializes into nextCursor; on the next call B's buffer already holds 10 so B is not refetched, and those items compete in the merge. They are not dropped, refetched, or forced onto page 1.

Each source can buffer up to about limit (plus one fetched page) items, all serialized as base64 JSON, so cursor size scales with sources and limit. Passing null still starts over, sources stay stateless, and buffered items are removed with shift so they are not repeated.
decode checks every configured source key and throws RangeError when an entry is missing. There is no partial initialization, no silent fallback to page 1, and no empty terminal page.
